summary.headline: DOMS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18.7% to INR604 crore, but West Asia raw-material inflation (15-20%) against only 4-5% price pass-through means Q1 FY27 margins will be under pressure.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 21.6% to INR2,326.4 crore and EBITDA rose 15.5% to INR402.6 crore, with EBITDA margin at 17.3% versus 18.2% in FY25. Q4 revenue grew 18.7% to INR604 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.7% from 17.3%, partly from baby hygiene seasonality and higher e-commerce costs at Uniclan. Management said raw-material costs have risen about 15-17% on average since the West Asia conflict, against pricing actions of roughly 4-5%, and expects Q1 FY27 margins to be slightly under pressure year-on-year. FY27 capex is guided at INR250-275 crore.

financial_highlights.value: INR377 crore: raw and packing material about INR140 crore, WIP about INR55 crore, rest finished goods and stock-in-trade

segments.name: Core stationery
segments.commentary: Grew about 19% in Q4 FY26, in line with company growth, led by office supplies, hobby and craft and back-to-school. Management denied channel stocking. Ball pens and highlighters drove office supplies growth.

segments.name: Uniclan (baby hygiene / diapers)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR203 crore (about 23% growth) at 8.6% EBITDA margin. Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 6.3% on higher e-commerce mix, selling and distribution costs and digital marketing. Long-term target is about 10% EBITDA margin and about 20% revenue growth.

segments.name: SKIDO
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR4.5 crore (60%+ YoY), driven by DOMS-branded backpacks. FY26 revenue rose from INR9 crore to INR14 crore. Plans new land and factory for capacity.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Direct branded exports grew at steady double-digit rates. Intercompany exports to FILA were lower than expected in FY26 due to US tariffs and weak European demand; management expects a recovery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 17-20%, including new 45-acre plant capacity ramping from H1 FY27.
Q1 FY27 margins expected to be slightly under pressure year-on-year; management calls this temporary, not a structural reset.
No definitive FY27 EBITDA margin guidance given; management reiterated long-term margin profile is intact.
Pricing actions so far about 4-5% against raw-material inflation of about 15-17% (weighted, to about 15 May). Further calibrated MRP and scheme changes are expected but timing is uncertain.
FY27 capex planned at INR250-275 crore, up from earlier INR225-250 crore, citing land purchases and some cost inflation.
Total 45-acre project capex estimated at INR850-1,000 crore over about 3 more years; first building due June 2027 with commercial production toward end of Q2 FY27.
Dividend policy remains about 10% of standalone profit; capex to be funded mainly from internal accruals, with room for some debt.
Seven SpA joint venture entity to be formed by end of June 2026.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR292 crore, versus an initial plan of INR225-250 crore. Spend covered the 45-acre plant, new land in Umargam and Jammu, and plant and machinery for writing instruments, moulding and adhesives.
45-acre facility: first building on track for June 2027 completion; commercial production expected toward end of Q2 FY27, starting with writing instruments.
Wooden pencil capacity is about 5.8 million pieces a day, rising to about 8 million once the new plant is fully ready.
Current operations span about 2 million sq ft built-up area; the 45-acre build-out is expected to roughly double manufacturing floor space over the next few years.
Capex intensity is expected to stay high for about 3 years, with similar annual spend for the 45-acre project.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as buoyant, supported by distribution reach, brand equity and new launches (pencil boxes, school bags, pens, mechanical pencils, stamp pads, highlighters).

Pricing: about 4-5% realised increase so far, taken mainly by cutting channel margins and schemes/discounts, applied across products. Management is avoiding aggressive MRP hikes to protect shelf space and market share.
Pen pricing: 5-pen packs were priced at INR30 (about INR6 per pen), so an MRP move to INR6 is a small step. Pencil MRP moved from INR55 to INR60 a pack in a past cycle.

Competition: Chinese and Vietnamese imports are a factor. A weaker rupee against the RMB makes imports costlier, which management sees as a share-gain opportunity. Natural hedge from USD-denominated imports and exports.

Distribution: directly serviceable universe about 225,000 stationery stores out of 300,000-350,000 in India. Management does not target store counts. Uniclan is expanding into general merchant (kirana) outlets.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q4 core stationery growth (about 19%) driven by channel stocking ahead of price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no channel stocking; primary and secondary sales are monitored closely. Growth reflected back-to-school demand. Price increases of about 4-5% were passed on across products.

qa_highlights.question: Could EBITDA margins fall below the 16.5-17.5% band if the crude-driven inflation persists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margins will be slightly under pressure year-on-year but called it temporary. It declined to give a definitive FY27 margin profile and said long-term margins should hold.

qa_highlights.question: What was the total price increase in the FY23 Ukraine-war cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give exact figures. It described a similar sequence (scheme and margin rationalisation first, then selective MRP increases) and said the earlier cycle also involved about 4-5% increases.

qa_highlights.question: What share of raw materials is crude-linked, and how much inventory is raw material?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% of the raw-material basket is directly crude-linked and about 30% indirectly linked. Of INR377 crore inventory, about INR140 crore is raw and packing material and about INR55 crore is WIP.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin compress while gross margin held steady in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin was steady. The compression came from higher selling, distribution and digital marketing costs as Uniclan's e-commerce mix grew, along with weaker fixed-cost absorption in baby hygiene.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue guidance and does it include the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated revenue growth is guided at 17-20% for FY27. Management confirmed this includes the new 45-acre plant capacity ramping from H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex guidance rise, and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase reflects new land parcels near Umargam and Jammu plus some cost inflation. Management said capex will be funded mainly from internal accruals, with room for prudent additional debt; FY26 free cash flow was limited.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR850-1,000 crore total for the 45-acre project separate from Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 45-acre project total (land, buildings and plant) is INR850-1,000 crore over about 3 more years. The INR292 crore FY26 capex is at company level and spans several projects.

risks_watch: Raw-material pass-through gap: about 15-17% cost inflation against 4-5% pricing, with Q1 FY27 margins under pressure. Watch the next pricing and MRP actions.
Crude linkage: about 40% of RM basket is directly crude-linked and about 30% indirectly. Volatility from the West Asia conflict could persist.
Uniclan margin dilution: Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 6.3% from about 7.5% a year earlier, driven by e-commerce spend. Long-term 10% target depends on scale.
Cash flow and funding: FY26 free cash flow was limited after higher capex, and FY27 capex of INR250-275 crore plus further 45-acre spend is planned. Watch debt levels and dividends.
Export dependence on FILA: intercompany exports fell in FY26 due to US tariffs and weak European demand. Recovery expected, but not yet visible.
Seven SpA JV formation expected by end of June 2026; SKIDO still at early stage (FY26 revenue about INR14 crore).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand, brand and capacity, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins. Management repeatedly declined to give FY27 margin numbers or detailed market-share and product-level capacity figures.
key_quotes: On an average, we have seen our raw material cost increase by approximately 15% to 17%, while the pricing actions taken so far are around 4% to 5%, which naturally creates a near-term gap.
But we do not view this as a structural revision of our margin – long-term margin profile, but more of temporary.
So, our universe to target would be about direct target, direct reach about 225,000 stationery stores.
The overriding principle is that any pricing action must be taken in a way that does not impact our market share or competitive positioning.
Yes. At consolidated level with the planned capacity expansion and the current demand trends, we expect revenue to grow by 17% to 20% in FY27.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 17-20% (midpoint 18.5%, held from prior call), tied to the 45-acre plant ramping from H1 FY27, but the 45-acre plant only starts commercial production toward end of Q2 FY27 and no order-book or contract figures were given, so backing is partial.
